summary.intent: Investigate the someguy IPFS sidecar state on staging, diagnose performance issues, upgrade Kubo, and set up proper routing configuration with CI improvements.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed someguy's IPNS endpoint as completely non-functional (hangs indefinitely), upgraded Kubo from v0.34.0 to v0.40.0 (verified with 83 E2E tests + load tests), removed someguy from staging and reverted to delegated-ipfs.dev, fixed Grafana Cloud 503s with a readiness poll, and added `build` commit type to release-please config to trigger version bumps.

repo: The `docker/` directory (docker-compose.staging.yml, Caddyfile, etc.) is generated during CI and copied to the VPS — it is committed to the repo under docker/ but not deployed via git directly.
someguy's `/routing/v1/providers/` endpoint works correctly, but `/routing/v1/ipns/` (both GET and PUT) hangs indefinitely — IPNS operations are completely broken in the deployed version.
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL defaults to https://delegated-ipfs.dev in the code (delegated-routing.client.ts line 24), but staging overrides this via .env.staging to http://someguy:8190.
The API's delegated routing publish is fire-and-forget (PR #308), so someguy IPNS timeouts don't cause HTTP errors — they silently fail after 3 retries x 10s = 30s wasted per publish.
release-please only triggers releases for `feat` and `fix` commit types by default — `build`, `chore`, and `ci` commits are non-user-facing and skipped.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances sleep when idle and return 503 'Your instance is loading' when woken — the provisioning step must poll /api/health before pushing dashboards.
someguy v0.11.1 is actually a patch ahead of the latest tagged release v0.11.0 — no newer version available to upgrade to.
Kubo v0.40's breaking changes (IPIP-524, IPIP-523) are all gateway-related; the API uses the RPC API exclusively (/api/v0/*) so no migration needed.

The throttle bypass uses X-Throttle-Bypass header with THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET — SDK E2E tests must set this env var or they get 429s. ThrottlerModule limits are hardcoded (10 req/s, 100 req/min), not relaxed by NODE_ENV.

code.finding: Fallback default URL is https://delegated-ipfs.dev when DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL env var is not set.
Throttle bypass guard checks X-Throttle-Bypass header against THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET — required for E2E/load tests to avoid 429s.
Load test harness records success:false on thrown exceptions — high error rates in metrics don't necessarily mean HTTP errors; can be SDK-level failures.
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190 is hardcoded in the deploy workflow env block — changes to .env.staging on the server get overwritten on each deploy.
Added changelog-sections config to include build commit type so infrastructure upgrades trigger version bumps via release-please.

workflow: When someguy was 'disabled' previously, the change didn't persist because the deploy workflow hardcodes DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL — server-side .env changes are overwritten on each deploy.

Running all vitest load test scenarios in one command causes them to run concurrently (sustained-load overlaps with others), producing misleading 522/error results — run scenarios individually for clean baselines.
NODE_ENV set in shell is overridden by .env file when NestJS ConfigModule loads it — must edit the file directly or pass via explicit env injection to override.
Copilot PR review suggestions: use `: "${VAR:?msg}"` syntax for env var validation in bash, and add early exit on non-retryable HTTP codes (401/403/404) in retry loops.
Use `--field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID` (not `-f`) when replying to PR review comments via gh api — the value must be an integer.
Kubo v0.40.1 is a Windows-only Go toolchain downgrade fix — not relevant for Linux deployments; v0.40.0 uses Go 1.26 with better memory/GC on Linux.

friction: someguy was believed to have been disabled previously, but the disable never persisted because deploy workflow hardcodes DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL — took significant investigation to determine the sidecar was active.
Initial load tests showed 74-95% error rates that looked like a performance problem but were actually someguy IPNS hangs (fire-and-forget failures) plus concurrent test scenario interference.
SDK E2E tests failed with 429s until the THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET env var was set — no documentation or .env.example entry for the load test suite.
The docker/ directory location wasn't obvious — the working directory during the session was tests/load, causing initial glob searches to find nothing.
`build` commit type doesn't trigger release-please by default — the Kubo upgrade PR merged without generating a release, requiring a follow-up config PR.
CodeRabbit described v0.40.1 as 'stability improvements' which was misleading — it's a Windows-only Go toolchain fix with no relevance to Linux deployments.
open_items: Post-phase-19 performance baselines not yet collected against staging — deferred until the latest deploy (with someguy removed) is live and stable.
someguy IPNS is broken — root cause not identified. May be a bug in someguy v0.11.x, an incompatibility with the Kubo version, or a configuration issue. Needs investigation before re-enabling.
TEE Worker still uses delegated-ipfs.dev directly — not routing through any self-hosted solution.
Kubo v0.40.0 deployed locally and staging compose updated, but staging hasn't been redeployed yet — PR #322 needs to merge and deploy to fully validate the upgrade in staging.
Load test throttle bypass secret not documented for SDK E2E test suite — tests/load and SDK E2E test suites both need THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET in their .env.example or README.
IPNS resolution improvement (Phase 19) goals not yet fully validated — need post-deploy staging load tests comparing someguy-off performance vs phase 18 delegated-ipfs.dev baseline.
